llm.summary: The skill is a coherent postal-mail integration, but it gives agents high-impact mail-sending and mail-disposal authority with only optional approval controls.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the capabilities: outbound physical mail, inbound forwarded document context, mailbox-address beta actions, webhooks, tags, notes, and sandbox testing are all disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifacts describe automatic standing rules where actions fire automatically and examples include junk mail discard; the beta mailbox workflow also lists shred, dispose, and return actions without requiring confirmation for irreversible handling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The install path is a remote MCP server or standard MCP remote bridge using bearer authentication; no local package code, hidden installer, or dependency chain is present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: External network access and bearer credentials are expected for this service, and the docs disclose agent-scoped keys, sandbox keys, dry_run, cost caps, and force_approval options.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The service can send real physical mail, batch mail, configure webhooks, keep persistent notes/tags, and in the mailbox beta request destructive physical-mail actions; these powers are significant and not consistently gated by mandatory human approval.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let an agent interact with real postal mail. Use sandbox or dry-run first, prefer agent-scoped test keys, set cost caps and force_approval, and require human review for sending legal/financial mail or for any discard, shred, dispose, or return-to-sender action.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The destructive mailbox concern is supported by artifact text: API actions include shred/dispose/return-to-sender and the decision framework/example allow discard of junk mail without a mandatory approval gate. This is purpose-related but under-scoped for irreversible physical mail handling.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The MAILBOX.md example and decision framework present automatic discard behavior as normal standing instructions, which could cause loss of important mail if classification is wrong.
[SQP-2] expected: Handling sensitive inbound document context and sending physical mail are core to the skill and are disclosed, but users still need to understand privacy, authorization, retention, and data-sharing implications before connecting real mail workflows.
[suspicious.exposed_secret_literal] expected: The static-scan secret finding appears to be placeholder documentation using values like sk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxx rather than an actual exposed credential.
